summary: Give the pages trims and retention free back to the filesystem: new stores use incremental auto-vacuum, released hourly in 2 MiB chunks

replay.detail: No claim replay or recovery behavior changes.

schema.detail: A newly created store sets PRAGMA auto_vacuum = INCREMENTAL before its first table. Existing stores keep auto_vacuum off (the pragma cannot change after tables exist) and are not rewritten. No tables, indexes, triggers or schema-version changes.

rules.detail: No checkpoint rules or digest changes; no coordinated member upgrade required.

compatibility.detail: No client, protocol or replication changes. Builds before this open an incremental store normally.

downtime.detail: No additional startup work. On an incremental store the hourly retention pass runs PRAGMA incremental_vacuum in 512-page background writes (about 35 ms each on a 32 GB store) with 50 ms between them; on any other store it reads one pragma and stops.

manual.detail: To make an existing store shrink, run one VACUUM with the daemon stopped at a deploy swap, as docs/st3/retention.md 'Giving space back' shows. It needs free disk about the size of the store and rewrites the whole file. PRAGMA auto_vacuum then answers 2. Without it nothing changes.

recovery.detail: Swap-back is supported: an older build opens an incremental store and simply leaves its free pages in the file.
